clue.text: Study of sets for game on borders of Germany

indicators.note: the borders of a country are its edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept

blocks.note: 'for' and 'to' are interchangeable in phrases like 'a ticket for London'
polo is a game played on horseback
the first and last letters of the country's name

explanation.surface: A sports pundit studying team line-ups for a match played near the German frontier.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sets' looks like groups of players, but it is the mathematician's word: TO + POLO + GY.
explanation.definitionFit: Topology is the branch of mathematics built on open sets, studying properties preserved under continuous deformation.

clue.text: Least exciting exam takes a minute

indicators.note: to take something is to hold it inside, so one piece is placed within the other

blocks.note: an exam is a test
taken as written
M is the standard abbreviation for minute

explanation.surface: A dull exam is made duller by taking only a minute.
explanation.walkthrough: A and M sit inside TEST, giving T-AM-EST.
explanation.definitionFit: Tame describes something dull or lacking spirit, and the superlative form means the least lively of all.

clue.text: Paramedics and ambulancemen first at appalling crash — hospital not admitted police vehicles

indicators.note: first points to the opening letter of each of the two neighbouring words
something not admitted is kept out, so these letters are dropped
something appalling is a mess, so the letters are thrown into a new order

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
taken as written
the opening letter of the word
taken as written, before losing a letter and being rearranged
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital, removed here

explanation.surface: Paramedics arrive first at a terrible road accident, where the police cars have not yet turned up.
explanation.walkthrough: CRASH loses its H to leave CRAS, which becomes CARS. Panda cars were the small British police patrol cars, once painted blue and white.
explanation.definitionFit: Panda car is the British nickname for a small police patrol vehicle, named for its two-tone livery.

clue.text: Cotton thread one’s placed in heart of galleon

indicators.note: to place one thing in another is to put it inside, so the pieces nest
the heart is the centre, so only the middle letters of the word are kept

the central three letters of the seven-letter word

explanation.walkthrough: IS goes into LLE, the middle of galleon, giving L-IS-LE.
explanation.definitionFit: Lisle is a fine, tightly twisted cotton thread, traditionally used for stockings and gloves.

clue.text: Succeeds in one’s career and travels a good distance

blocks.note: first meaning: does well in life
second meaning: journeys a long way

explanation.walkthrough: The same phrase is used figuratively for success and literally for a long journey.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom describes someone who will achieve a great deal, while the literal sense covers covering many miles.

clue.text: Briefly ask advice of diplomat

indicators.note: briefly means cut short, so the final letter is dropped

blocks.note: to consult someone is to ask their advice; the last letter goes

explanation.surface: Someone seeks a quick word of advice from an embassy official.
explanation.walkthrough: CONSULT loses its last letter.
explanation.definitionFit: A consul is a government official posted abroad to protect citizens and trade, a member of the diplomatic service.

clue.text: Agreed on a review of drink

indicators.note: a review goes back over material and reworks it, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.surface: A panel reaches agreement on its verdict about a drink.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Review' suggests a critic's verdict, but it signals rearranging the nine letters before it.

clue.text: Novelist suggests photographic session

clue.text: Scotland Yard can’t be missing out the Sabbath!

these four letters are removed

explanation.walkthrough: Take C, A, N and T from SCOTLAND YARD to leave SOLDYARD, then rearrange. Scotland Yard is the headquarters of London's Metropolitan Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Christians call Sunday the Lord's Day, their weekly day of rest and worship, equivalent to the Sabbath.

clue.text: Cabinet member, one entering church

explanation.walkthrough: I goes inside MINSTER, after its third letter. A minister of religion is a church figure too, which helps the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: The cabinet is made up of senior government ministers, each running a department of state.

clue.text: Cat from jungle originally — one keeping watch endlessly

without an end, the word loses its final letter

blocks.note: the opening letter of the word
a means one
a guard keeps watch; the last letter goes

clue.text: French busy in off-licence

indicators.note: in tells us the letters sit inside the following words

blocks.note: found running across the hyphenated word

explanation.definitionFit: Flic is the French slang word for a policeman, just as busy is British slang for one.

clue.text: Possibly gets a coach

clue.text: 1001 golfers turned round for cineastes

the letters taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The number is not a quantity but two Roman numerals, joined to the golfers before the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Cineastes are enthusiasts of cinema, so regular cinema audiences are a close match.

clue.text: It’s not so sensible to read FT out of order

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: The setter's nod to the paper the puzzle appears in: the FT is the Financial Times.
explanation.definitionFit: Daft is British for silly or foolish, and the comparative means less sensible than before.

clue.text: Now melted — due to what boiling?

clue.text: Female spies accepting praise

blocks.note: the CIA is the American intelligence agency

clue.text: Night-time beneficial to church as energy source in the Marvel universe

blocks.note: night-time is the dark

CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A comic-book plot in which night-time is a power source helping a church.
explanation.walkthrough: CE, the Church of England, is a standard crossword abbreviation.

clue.text: Moving pictures detected creaking in the knees

blocks.note: the letters taken as written

explanation.walkthrough: 'Moving pictures' reads as films, but the first word is the signal and the second is the letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Crepitus is the medical term for a grating or crackling sound from joints, as in arthritic knees.

clue.text: In the pink, having got up and tucked in

explanation.walkthrough: 'In the pink' suggests good health, but here it is meant literally, as a colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Roseate means rose-coloured or pinkish, so a roseate thing is literally pink in hue.

clue.text: Swimmers sleep over endlessly

blocks.note: the word without its last letter

explanation.walkthrough: SLEE(P) turned over.
explanation.definitionFit: Eels are long snake-like fish, and any fish is a swimmer in crossword language.

the letters taken as written
